card.name: Latin abbreviations before the period
card.fires_on: The word "et" right after an author surname in citations ("Gallagher et al."), and "etc" or other abbreviations just before a period. It marks the point where a short abbreviation is about to be finished by "." or "al".

modes.label: Author et al.
modes.description: "et" following a researcher's surname in a citation.
modes.example: Assumptions on the biodistribution based on data from Gallagher<< et>> al. 1 and Jones et al

modes.label: etc. in lists
modes.description: "etc" closing an example list inside parentheses, before the period.
modes.example: biologic or colloidal fluids (e.g., blood products, protein solutions,<< etc>>.) are not recommended

modes.label: Other dotted abbreviations
modes.description: Part of a dated or ordinal abbreviation just before its final period or letters.
modes.example: After the creation of the Roman Empire in 27 B<<.C>>.E., the Senate became weakened

card.plain: It fires on abbreviations like "et al." and "etc." just before they finish.
